newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dell sees above industry average growth.
newsitem.headline: Dell sees above industry average growth.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp, a direct marketer of computer systems, expects above industry average growth rate, with Asia a major revenue generator, company officials said on Monday.
"We can expect to continue to grow two to three times the industry growth rate," chairman and chief executive officer, Michael Dell told Reuters after a news conference.
"We have great opportunities this year. I think we are going to grow very rapidly. It's going to be a good year," Dell said.
The founder of Dell Computer was in Singapore to launch its Dimension desktop family of personal computers.
"Over time, Asia-Pacific including Japan, could represent 20-30 percent of our revenue," Dell said.

Dell said he was quite pleased with the success of the company in the Asian countries it was operating from -- Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan and South Korea.

Dell Computers saw sales increase over three times the industry rate, rising 57 percent to US$2.4 billion in the fourth quarter ended February 2, 1997 while net income for fiscal 1997 grew 91 percent to US$518 million.
In the last quarter of its fiscal year, which ended on February 2, Asia contributed about six percent of Dell Computer's revenue, Dell said.
Growth strategies included expanding product lines, using the internet to sell its computers and expanding into workstations, server and services, Dell said.
Sales via the internet had received "good response" according to the company's Asia-Pacific president, Phillip Kelly.
"We see 10-20 percent of Asia Pacific volumes coming across the internet by year end," Kelly said.
Dell said its Dimension line would allow the company to tap into the growing market for small to medium sized companies as well as experienced computer users.
Its strategy of direct selling was the key to the strong growth of the company, which maintained operating margins of 10 percent of total revenue, Dell said.
"We see almost no financial risk, unlike companies with indirect sales. Last year our return on investment capital was 154 percent, much higher than the industry," he said.
By selling directly to customers, Dell Computers was also able to maintain a faster inventory flow minimize obsolescence, Dell said.
He said the company's goal was to see contributions from notebooks and servers grow to 40-45 percent percent of revenue from 26 percent last quarter.

Notebooks and server sales grew 84 percent and 310 percent respectively. Dell said he saw desktop sales, which grew by 62 percent last quarter, remaining the main revenue generator at about 74 percent.
Plans were under way to gear up its sole Asian manufacturing plant in Penang, Malaysia to producing at full capacity within the next 24 months, Dell said.
